chunks: And it is narrated from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī that he said:
Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to me: “Say in the sajdah of gratitude one hundred times: ‘Shukran, shukran,’ and if you wish: ‘Afwan, afwan.’”

key_terms.سَجْدَةِ: the prostration performed here as an act of devotion
key_terms.شُكْرًا: an expression of thankfulness recited in the prostration
key_terms.عَفْوًا: an expression meaning pardon, used here as an alternative recitation
key_terms.مِائَةَ: one hundred, indicating the number of repetitions

ai.seo_question: What should be said in Sajdat al-Shukr according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a recommended dhikr to be recited in Sajdat al-Shukr. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام instructs saying “Shukran, shukran” one hundred times, and permits “Afwan, afwan” as an alternative expression in that prostration.
